topsis.title: Distances to A+ and A−
topsis.caption: Closer to A+ and farther from A− gives a higher C.
topsis.projectionNote: Drawn on the two heaviest criteria; D and C use all criteria.
topsis.planeCaption: Top left is best. C is the same along each ray.

steps.s1: Each alternative is a point: its weighted normalized values on two criteria.
steps.s2: The ideal A+ takes the best value of each criterion, the anti-ideal A− the worst.
steps.s3: D+ and D− are the selected alternative's distances to the ideal and the anti-ideal.
steps.s4: Place each alternative at (D+, D−): its two distances become its coordinates.
steps.s5: Relative closeness C = D− / (D+ + D−) is the same along each ray; top left is best.

steps.s1: Contrast: σ, the standard deviation of each criterion's normalized values.
steps.s2: Conflict: Σ(1 − ρ) is large when a criterion correlates weakly or negatively with the others.
steps.s3: Information content C = σ × Σ(1 − ρ): a criterion that varies and disagrees carries more.
steps.s4: Weight w = C / ΣC: the same bars divided by the total, so the weights add up to 1.

saw.title: Every part of the score has a criterion

vikor.title: Group utility or the largest regret: v sets the balance
vikor.caption: Below the dashed line Q stays within DQ of the leader; without an acceptable advantage those alternatives form the compromise set.

edas.title: Better or worse than the average, criterion by criterion
edas.caption: Right of the line: weighted distance above the average; left: below it; AS divides each by the largest SP or SN.

sd.title: Wider spread, more weight

critic.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
critic.sigma: Contrast: the sample standard deviation of each normalized column.
critic.correlation: Conflict between criteria: the Pearson correlation of every pair of normalized columns.
critic.conflict: Total conflict of each criterion: the sum of 1 minus its correlation with every criterion.
critic.information: Information content of each criterion: its standard deviation times its total conflict.
critic.informationTotal: Total information content over all criteria.
critic.weights: Weights: each criterion's share of the total information content.

entropy.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
entropy.proportionsSum: Shares: each raw value divided by its column's total. Criterion types are not used.
entropy.proportionsMinmax: Shares: each normalized value divided by its column's total.
entropy.entropy: Entropy of each criterion: 1 when the shares are equal, lower the more uneven they are.
entropy.diversification: Degree of diversification: 1 minus the entropy, the information a criterion carries.
entropy.weights: Entropy weights: each criterion's share of the total diversification.

topsis.normalized: Vector normalization: each value divided by the length of its column.
topsis.weighted: Weighted normalized matrix: each column multiplied by its weight.
topsis.idealBest: Ideal solution A+: the best weighted value on each criterion (the maximum for benefit, the minimum for cost).
topsis.idealWorst: Anti-ideal solution A-: the worst weighted value on each criterion.
topsis.distanceBest: Euclidean distance D+ of each alternative from the ideal solution.
topsis.distanceWorst: Euclidean distance D- of each alternative from the anti-ideal solution.
topsis.closeness: Closeness coefficient C = D- / (D+ + D-). A higher value ranks higher.

equal.weights: Equal weights: every criterion gets 1 / n.

saw.normalizedLinearMax: Linear max normalization: each value divided by the column maximum, or for a cost criterion the column minimum divided by the value, so the best value is 1.
saw.normalizedSum: Sum normalization: each value divided by its column total; a cost criterion uses 1 / x first, so the shares add up to 1.
saw.weighted: Contributions: each normalized value multiplied by its criterion weight.
saw.scores: Score S: the sum of an alternative's contributions. A higher value ranks higher.

vikor.best: Best value f* of each criterion: the maximum for a benefit, the minimum for a cost.
vikor.worst: Worst value f− of each criterion: the other end of its column.
vikor.weightedDistance: Weighted distance d to the best value: 0 at the best, the criterion weight at the worst.
vikor.groupUtility: Group utility S: the sum of an alternative's distances. A lower value is better.
vikor.individualRegret: Individual regret R: an alternative's largest single distance. A lower value is better.
vikor.q: Compromise index Q: S and R rescaled to 0 to 1 and mixed by v. A lower value ranks higher.
vikor.threshold: Advantage threshold DQ = 1 / (m - 1): the Q gap the first alternative needs over the second.

edas.average: Average solution AV: the mean of each criterion over all alternatives.
edas.pda: Positive distance PDA: how much better than the average an alternative is, as a share of the average.
edas.nda: Negative distance NDA: how much worse than the average an alternative is, as a share of the average.
edas.weightedPda: Weighted positive distances w PDA: what each criterion adds to SP.
edas.weightedNda: Weighted negative distances w NDA: what each criterion adds to SN.
edas.sp: SP: the sum of an alternative's weighted positive distances.
edas.sn: SN: the sum of an alternative's weighted negative distances.
edas.nsp: NSP = SP / max SP: 1 for the alternative furthest above the average.
edas.nsn: NSN = 1 - SN / max SN: 0 for the alternative furthest below the average.
edas.scores: Appraisal score AS = (NSP + NSN) / 2. A higher value ranks higher.

sd.normalized: Min-max normalization: each column is rescaled to the range 0 to 1, with cost criteria reversed so that 1 is always the best value.
sd.sigma: Spread: the sample standard deviation of each normalized column. Criterion types do not change it.
sd.weights: Weights: each criterion's share of the total spread.

codes.alternatives-count-mismatch: The number of alternative names does not match the number of rows.
codes.value-out-of-range: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is too large or too small to compute with. Rescale {{criterion}} (another unit) so its values lie between 10⁻¹⁰⁰ and 10¹⁰⁰.
codes.constant-column: Every alternative has the same value on {{criterion}}, so it cannot tell them apart.
codes.non-positive-value: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is {{value}}. This method divides by the values, so each must be above 0.
codes.negative-value: {{alternative}} on {{criterion}} is {{value}}. Raw data (sum) needs values of 0 or more; choose Min-max to use negative values.
codes.invalid-weight: Enter a number for the weight of {{criterion}}.
codes.negative-weight: The weight of {{criterion}} is {{value}}. Weights cannot be negative.
codes.weights-sum: Weights sum to {{value}}, they must sum to 1.
codes.non-positive-average: The average of {{criterion}} is {{value}}. EDAS divides by each criterion's average, so it must be above 0.

critic.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its CRITIC weight is 0.
critic.few-alternatives: With fewer than 4 alternatives the correlations are unstable. Read the CRITIC weights with care.
critic.no-conflict-equal-weights: The criteria that vary carry no conflict with each other (only one varies, or they move together), so they share the weight equally.
critic.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so there is no information to weigh. Equal weights are used instead.
critic.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.

entropy.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its Entropy weight is 0.
entropy.zeros-in-column: {{criterion}} contains zeros, which can inflate its weight.
entropy.two-alternatives-minmax: With 2 alternatives, min-max gives every criterion that is not constant the same weight.
entropy.dominant-weight: {{criterion}} takes more than half of the weight, so check whether its spread is real.
entropy.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.

topsis.zero-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is 0, so it does not affect the ranking.
topsis.zero-distance: Some alternatives coincide with both the ideal and the anti-ideal solution. They get a closeness of 0.5.

vikor.constant-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is the same, so it adds nothing to S or R.
vikor.equal-group-utility: Every alternative has the same S, so Q comes from R alone and reaches at most 1 − v, which can make C1 harder to meet.
vikor.equal-regret: Every alternative has the same R, so Q comes from S alone and reaches at most v, which can make C1 harder to meet.
vikor.no-spread: Every alternative has the same S and the same R, so all get Q = 0.
vikor.tie-for-first: More than one alternative has the lowest Q; they are listed in input order and all are in the compromise set.

edas.constant-column: Every value of {{criterion}} is the same, so it adds nothing to SP or SN.
edas.negative-values: {{criterion}} has negative values. EDAS measures distance as a share of the average, so the result depends on where zero is.
edas.small-average: The average of {{criterion}} is close to 0 next to its values, so its distances grow very large and it can decide the ranking even with a small weight.
edas.no-spread: No alternative is above or below the average on a weighted criterion, so every alternative gets AS = 0.5.

sd.constant-column: {{criterion}} has the same value for every alternative, so its SD weight is 0.
sd.near-constant-column: {{criterion}} varies only by a rounding-sized amount, yet min-max stretches it to 0 to 1 and gives it a full weight. Check whether the difference is real.
sd.two-alternatives: With 2 alternatives, every criterion that is not constant gets the same SD weight.
sd.all-constant-equal-weights: Every criterion is constant, so equal weights are used instead.
